clue.text: Calling out, get lost in Oxford?

indicators.note: calling out means saying a word aloud, so the solver writes the word that sounds like the one spoken

parts.note: shoo is what you say to drive someone away: get lost!

explanation.surface: Someone shouting about getting lost in the city of Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the city, but the question mark points to the lace-up style of footwear named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a classic laced leather style of footwear, given here as an example.

clue.text: Erupt violently, punching 100 square metres to make hole

indicators.note: punching means one piece is driven into the middle of another

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of land area equal to 100 square metres

indicators.note: violently suggests the letters of erupt being thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Something bursts out forcefully, smashing through a patch of ground to leave a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: An are is a metric unit of land area, rarely met outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is an opening or gap, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Boasted striking top is worn

indicators.note: striking off the top means knocking away the first letter of the word

parts.note: to boast is to brag, so boasted is bragged

explanation.surface: A braggart's showy top has now become shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragged clothes are tattered and frayed from long use, a synonym for worn.

clue.text: Doesn't go barefoot as comfort for supplicants

definitions.meaning: someone who doesn't go barefoot ... on: read as two words, ...
kneeling cushions in church pews ease the knees of those at prayer

explanation.surface: Wearing something on your feet is likened to a comfort for those praying.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: split the answer as HAS SOCKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassocks are firm cushions for kneeling on in church, a comfort for those praying.

clue.text: Leading 17 across requiring much effort

parts.note: a team that is leading is up, ahead in the game
the entry at 17 across is a word for a versifier; Geoffrey Hill was an English one

explanation.surface: Being ahead of the rest of the poets demands real effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 across is the theme word for a verse writer; Geoffrey Hill was an English one.
explanation.definitionFit: An uphill task is a strenuous, difficult one, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: My turn — pipe down!

parts.note: your go is your turn in a game
sh is the word used to tell someone to be quiet

explanation.surface: A player claims their turn and tells everyone to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive, but it is the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, so one can stand for the other.

clue.text: May bores drink with an old pedlar?

indicators.note: bores means drills into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: cha is a colloquial word for tea
Theresa May was the Prime Minister, PM

explanation.surface: Someone called May tediously goes on about drinking with an elderly hawker.
explanation.walkthrough: May is Theresa May, the British Prime Minister, so PM bores into CHA + AN. George Chapman was also an Elizabethan poet, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapman was a travelling dealer in small goods in earlier centuries, a historical word.

clue.text: Victor Hugo initially abandons flowering plant

indicators.note: abandons means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: a victor is a winner, a champion

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of Hugo

explanation.surface: Victor Hugo, the French novelist, gives up on a plant in bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor Hugo' looks like the novelist, but the words split: Victor gives CHAMPION, which loses Hugo's first letter. Thomas Campion was also a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Campions are wildflowers of the pink family, so this names one kind of flowering plant.

clue.text: "Old King Cole" artist's covered

indicators.note: covered means the answer lies concealed within the run of letters of the words given

explanation.surface: The artist who painted Old King Cole has the subject covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old King Cole' looks like the nursery rhyme, but Old King is the definition. Edward Lear, the nonsense poet, was also an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's King Lear is an aged British monarch, so he fits an old king.

clue.text: Artisan might put out stocks sold wrongly

indicators.note: stocks means holds within, so one group of letters keeps the other inside it
put out means disordered, so the letters of might are thrown into a new arrangement
wrongly means the letters of sold are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A craftsman might clear out goods that were sold improperly.
explanation.walkthrough: GMITH (might reworked) stocks OLDS (sold reworked) after its G. Oliver Goldsmith is a theme poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A goldsmith is a craftsman working precious metal, so an example of an artisan.

clue.text: Sad relics arranged in storage medium

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Mournful mementos are laid out in a storage space.
explanation.definitionFit: A laserdisc is an early optical format for holding video, an example of a storage medium.

clue.text: Tender from bash

definitions.meaning: legal tender is money, and Britain's currency unit is one example
to bash is to strike heavily and repeatedly

explanation.surface: Something offered comes from a heavy blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterling's unit is legal tender, and to beat hard is another sense of the same word.

clue.text: P&O crossing popular still

indicators.note: crossing means spanning over, so one piece sits around the other

parts.note: P&O, the shipping company, gives the letters P and O
something hot is in demand, popular

explanation.surface: A P&O ferry crossing is still popular.
explanation.walkthrough: P&O is a British ferry and cruise line, a natural fit for a crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single frozen image from a film, a picture taken as a snapshot.

clue.text: Small bird's young daughter leaves baby

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so the letter departs from the word

parts.note: a duckling is a young duck
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A little bird's chick abandons its infant.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Suckling was a Cavalier poet, another theme entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A suckling is a baby still feeding at the breast, an unweaned infant.

clue.text: Pretty inclusive of English family member

indicators.note: inclusive of means containing, so one word holds the letter

parts.note: pretty means pleasant, nice

explanation.surface: An attractive relative from England.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a relative, so a member of the family.

clue.text: Roman leader's attempt to get back in senate

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: to have a pop at something is to have an attempt at it

indicators.note: back in means the last letter of senate

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman ruler tries to return to the Senate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman leader' suggests an emperor, but it is the head of the Roman Catholic Church. Alexander Pope is the theme poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bishop of Rome heads the Roman Catholic Church, so he leads Roman Catholics.

clue.text: Poles following ebb of Polish streams

indicators.note: following means the poles come after the other piece
an ebb flows back, so the word for polish is read backwards

parts.note: to polish is to rub
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish flows ebbing away, sounding like rivers of Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, but it is the verb. Robert Burns is the theme poet.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and northern England a small stream is a burn, a regional word.

clue.text: Shopped and risked money, ready to fail

parts.note: to bet is to stake money on an outcome

indicators.note: to fail means to break down, so the letters of ready collapse into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone went shopping and gambled, prepared for disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: READY rearranged gives RAYED. 'Shopped' is British slang for informed on someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them, so it means sold out or betrayed.

clue.text: Fit clothes round anything put across here?

definitions.note: nearly every across entry in this grid is a versifier, so this names whatever is entered across

indicators.note: clothes means dresses, wraps around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A tailor fits garments around whatever someone is putting on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the grid: almost every across entry is a writer of verse, the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The across answers are writers of verse, so the theme word describes whatever goes across.

clue.text: Most recent cutting snaps materials

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: snaps are photographs, pics
the most recent is the last

explanation.surface: The latest clippings of photographs make the materials.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastics are synthetic polymers used for manufacturing, a kind of material.

clue.text: Painter to resist making amendments

indicators.note: making amendments means altering, so the letters of to resist are reordered

explanation.surface: An artist refuses to revise their work.
explanation.walkthrough: Dante Gabriel Rossetti was both painter and poet; his sister Christina was a poet too.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti was a Pre-Raphaelite artist, so an example of a painter.

clue.text: Mathematician's line is able to divide group

indicators.note: to divide means to split apart, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: a set is a group of things that belong together
can means is able

explanation.surface: A mathematician's line is capable of splitting a group.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a secant is a straight line cutting a curve at two points.

clue.text: Means to lift fallen arches, a bit revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning around, so that portion is read backwards
a bit means only a portion of the words given is used

explanation.surface: A way to raise collapsed foot arches, somewhat radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fallen arches' looks like a foot complaint; the letters ENARC are in it, and read backwards. Hart Crane is the theme poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A crane is a machine for hoisting heavy loads, a way to raise things.

clue.text: Jug with extra ice in

definitions.meaning: a drink with more ice in it is colder

explanation.surface: A pitcher with plenty of ice added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jug' looks like a pitcher, but it is slang for prison, as is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The cooler is slang for jail, and a drink with more ice has a lower temperature.

clue.text: Was a disheartened Dave Cameron his work?

definitions.text: Was a disheartened Dave Cameron his work?

parts.words: Was a disheartened Dave Cameron his work?
parts.note: take the heart out of Dave and add Cameron to give the title of a famous fourteenth-century Italian story collection; the clue asks for its author

explanation.surface: It asks whether a dejected David Cameron, the former British Prime Minister, was this person's creation.
explanation.walkthrough: Dave without its middle letters is DE; add CAMERON and you get the Decameron, the Italian story collection whose author is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Boccaccio wrote the Decameron, so it is his work.

clue.text: Rolls heading for Barmouth, a resort on the up

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of Barmouth
on the up means rising, so in a down entry the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: Bread rolls heading to Barmouth, a seaside town in Wales that is improving.
explanation.definitionFit: Baps are soft round bread rolls, a British word.

clue.text: British art institution, say, a non-starter

indicators.note: a non-starter is without its start, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: to state is to say

explanation.surface: A British gallery is described as a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: Nahum Tate, a Poet Laureate, is the theme connection.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate is the group of national galleries in Britain, a famous art institution.

clue.text: Dry sandwiches a cold delicacy

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the outer letters enclose the rest

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, dry
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Plain sandwiches are a chilled gourmet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delicacy' looks like a fine food beside sandwiches, but it means sensitivity.
explanation.definitionFit: Tact is sensitivity in dealing with others, and delicacy has that sense too.

clue.text: Rebuffed sellers holding back buyer?

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece sits within the other
rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the word for sellers is read backwards

parts.note: reps are sales representatives
the end is the back of something

explanation.surface: Salespeople turned away are keeping back a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Spender is the theme poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who parts with money for goods is a purchaser, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Kiss overwhelms a firm, vain fellow

indicators.note: overwhelms means covers over, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a peck is a quick kiss
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A kiss swamps a conceited man in business.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Love Peacock is the theme writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Peacocks strut and display, so the bird's name is used for a showy, conceited man.
